newsitem.title: FRANCE: Chirac sees euro "stability pact" deal.
newsitem.headline: Chirac sees euro "stability pact" deal.

text.p: French President Jacques Chirac said on Thursday he believed there would be agreement on the "stability pact" on budgetary discipline between countries in the future euro currency zone, perhaps at the Dublin EU summit.

"I am sure we'll get there, maybe even tomorrow in Dublin," Chirac said in a television interview. He also said those who were calling for a devaluation of the franc versus the German mark were wrong and that such a move would amount to "the rupture of the Franco-German partnership".

"Those who claim that the franc should be devalued against the mark are wrong, firstly because it would be inacceptable for the Germans and because it would blow European construction apart," Chirac said.
"It would be more than a crisis. It would be a rupture of the Franco-German partnership and then we would have to face a major European crisis," he said.

European Union leaders meet in Dublin on Friday and Saturday and finance ministers from the 15 EU countries were meeting on Thursday night to try to hammer out a deal on a German-proposed pact on public deficit control in countries using the euro.

Concerning the powers of the future European central bank, Chirac said: "The German Bundesbank has to face up to a government. The European central bank will have to face up to a responsible political institution".
